ui.teamBridge.invitations.consent.bridge.value: Accepting lets your agent read and post in this conversation from now on. It sees every message and decides whether to reply; an @-mention means it should reply. You can change how often it wakes, or mute it, from the conversation’s ⋯ menu.

ui.teamBridge.invitations.consent.bridge.context_note: Desktop Team Bridge Invitations view. A teammate added the reader's own AI agent (chief of staff) to a channel or group; the agent cannot join until its owner accepts. The consent statement the owner agrees to by pressing Accept; the key names the participation version it is consent to (bridge_agent_participation_v2), so ANY change to this English text before it ships needs review, and after it ships needs a new version and a new key. Keep every fact: from now on the agent can read the conversation's messages AND post there; it is woken for EVERY message and judges for itself whether to reply; an @-mention means a reply is expected; the owner can change how often it is woken or mute it, and the place to do that is the conversation's ⋯ (more options) menu — keep the ⋯ glyph as is. 'Mute it' here means the agent is never woken, not even by an @-mention.
ui.teamBridge.invitations.consent.bridge.context_length: Two or three sentences; permit wrapping.

findings.detail: '唤醒你的智能体的时机' stacks two 的 ('the timing of waking your agent'); '何时唤醒你的智能体' or '唤醒智能体：' is lighter. A noun-phrase heading over the rows is idiomatic in zh-CN menus and the meaning is exact; accepted unchanged. ZH-N1 no longer applies: agentNotify.mute changed to '从不（已静音）', a state.

prior_findings_rechecked: ZH-N1 resolved by the source change (mute is now '从不（已静音）').
